complexity.notes: The logic is correct but does redundant work: maxDepth re-walks each subtree once per ancestor, which is what makes the worst case quadratic on a skewed tree. A single bottom-up pass that ||returns each subtree's height from the recursion (or a sentinel like -1 once an imbalance is found)|| would be O(n) time and short-circuits early on unbalanced trees. On the benchmark ladder the tree is always complete, so this stays at O(n log n) and never trips CPython's recursion limit, but on the generalized problem a fully skewed tree would overflow the recursion stack at depth n.
complexity.summary: Top-down check: at every node it recursively computes the height of both subtrees with maxDepth, compares them, and recurses into the children, so subtree heights are recomputed at each ancestor.
